outcomes: Unroll a recurrent state over time
Derive and check BPTT gradients through shared recurrent weights
Trace LSTM input, forget, output, and candidate paths
Distinguish teacher-forced one-step evaluation from free-running inference on a later contiguous segment

recurrent-neural-network.name: recurrent neural network
recurrent-neural-network.definition: A network that reuses parameters while carrying state from one time step to the next.
recurrent-neural-network.explanation: A basic RNN combines the current input with its previous hidden state, applies a nonlinearity, and produces a new state. The same weights operate at every time step, allowing variable-length sequences and a compact form of memory. The state is a summary, not a literal storage of every observation. Saturating nonlinearities and repeated multiplication can make long-range gradients shrink or grow, limiting what a simple RNN can learn.

bptt.name: backpropagation through time
bptt.definition: Reverse-mode differentiation through an unrolled recurrent computation.
bptt.explanation: BPTT treats each time step as another use of the same recurrent cell. The forward pass stores states; the reverse pass starts at later losses and carries a gradient backward through each recurrent edge. Contributions from every use accumulate into the shared parameter gradients. Truncated BPTT stops after a fixed window to bound memory and computation, changing how far credit can travel. The project uses the full short training prefix so the derivation stays visible.

lstm.name: long short-term memory
lstm.definition: A gated recurrent cell with a separate memory state and controlled update paths.
lstm.explanation: An LSTM computes input, forget, and output gates with sigmoids plus a candidate value with tanh. The forget gate scales old cell memory, the input gate scales the candidate update, and the output gate controls exposed hidden state. Its additive cell-state path can preserve gradients better than repeatedly applying one saturating recurrent transformation. LSTMs still need careful optimization and do not automatically solve arbitrary long-horizon forecasting.

teacher-forcing.name: teacher forcing
teacher-forcing.definition: Supplying true previous sequence values as model inputs during training or explicitly teacher-forced evaluation.
teacher-forcing.explanation: Teacher forcing supplies the true previous value or token to predict the next one. It is standard during sequence training and may also be chosen explicitly for one-step evaluation, where it isolates conditional next-step quality and prevents model errors from becoming later inputs. Free-running inference instead feeds each generated output back as the next input, so errors can accumulate. Results from these settings answer different questions and must be labeled. This chapter reports explicitly teacher-forced one-step MSE; it does not claim free-running forecast quality.
